A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dr.APP study. Their complete text, equations, five figures, two tables, references, and doctor/patient survey appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulated medical-consultation experiments, diagnostic evaluations, and human assessments, with outcomes in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original consultation experiments, diagnostic results, confidence analyses, and human evaluations reported in v2.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.7 retain the same MSD-grounded retrieval, disease-probability estimation, simulated responses, entropy-based question selection, and human-centric communication procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ReMeDi-derived simulated consultations, reporting coverage of 72 diseases across 18 specialties. No datasets, tasks, populations, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains LLaMA-70B, Claude-3, GPT-4o, QWen-72B, and DeepSeek-v3 alongside the same APP variants. Table 2 retains the same model comparators and original real-world dialogues.

E3.justification: Both retain the 100-case selection, six-round multi-turn evaluation, three expert evaluators, and five non-medical participants reviewing 20 cases with five dialogue versions each. Metrics, randomized presentation, and Appendix A rating rubrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: The allergic-rhinitis case study in Figure 3 and confidence analyses across iterations in Figures 4–5 are identical. Neither version adds ablations, robustness tests, or other supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain the same average-score reporting and evaluator information. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: All values and rankings in Tables 1–2 and results depicted in Figures 3–5 match. For example, APP-DeepSeek-v3 retains overall diagnostic scores of 3.35 for one-shot and 3.59 for multi-turn evaluation in Table 1.

T1.justification: The probability definitions, Bayesian derivation, entropy expression, and selection rule in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, mathematical corrections, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about human-centric medical dialogue, grounded Bayesian reasoning, the consultation benchmark, and improved diagnostic and user-experience outcomes.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including greedy question selection potentially reaching local minima, dependence on guideline coverage, and the need for real-world clinical validation.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same local symptom-description retrieval, DeepSeek-v3 persona construction, five candidate questions, and two to five simulated responses per question. Implementation and resource-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference entries, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning match. Reference reflow does not introduce or remove research.

P1.justification: v3 adds an asterisk identifying Jiazhen Pan as the corresponding author and a corresponding-author footnote. Apart from version-header metadata, the prose, terminology, and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adjusts vertical spacing and page/column breaks, removes printed page numbers, and starts Appendix A on a separate page. Figures and tables retain their content and design, with some placement shifts.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and complete survey appendices. Identifying the corresponding author and adjusting layout do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
